flags.t: Hwy 5 100 m W: no hunting or shooting on or across the road allowance of a numbered highway or 2 lane public road, 15 m (16 yd) each side of the centre line (synopsis page 10, 99%).
Inside the 400 m single projectile ban beside Hwy 5 (Coquihalla): shotgun with shot only, no rifle, slug or .22 (synopsis, 99%). Zone drawn from the road atlas (estimate).

R2A-deer-atv-0004.pressureWhy: Busier: within 1 km of a paved road (estimate).
R2A-deer-atv-0004.parkWhat: where the truck road ends (unnamed paved road); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle)

evidence.t: Deer here are black tailed deer, the coast form of mule deer: the synopsis calls them "mule (black-tailed) deer" (99%, Rule Book: Region 2 Lower Mainland).
No official deer winter range within 500 m, so the top score here is 8 of 11. This score leans on cutblocks, burns, habitat zone and aspect.
Cutblock harvested 2016 (10 years old), right here.
Burn from 2021 (fire V10859, 52 ha), 640 m N.
Habitat zone Coastal Western Hemlock (CWHms3): coast forest, where black tailed deer are among the most common large mammals (95%) and use logged ground often (80%) (lesson: Wet forests).
SW facing slope, 12 degrees: sun melts snow first.
Private fields 1.6 km S: deer feed on field edges (fields are private).
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).

100% of the stretch in grouse forest zones (BWBS, CWH, ESSF, ICH, IDF, MS, SBPS, SBS).
3 cutblocks touch the road (30 years old or less): edges and clover.
17 wetlands, lakes or creeks along the road: riparian edges.
